reply_text:
The quoted words are on the Carscoops page as quoted, but I would leave the candidate out, because it fails part 2 of the rule.

**1. Page check.** The page opened. It is a Carscoops news report by Sergiu Tudose, dated Nov. 11, 2016 9:00 pm EST (the page's metadata gives 2016-11-12 02:00 UTC). It credits Electrek. The quote is there with no differences: Huang said Tesla's system is "basically five years ahead. Anybody who's talking about 2021... that's just a non-starter anymore. And I think that's probably the most significant bit in the automotive industry. I just don't – anybody who is talking about autonomous capabilities in 2020 and 2021 is at the moment re-evaluating in a very significant way." The report does not say when or where Huang said this. The 2016-11-10 earnings-call date comes from the search run and is not on the page. This is coverage, not a transcript, so at best it would be "pass, coverage only".

**2. Admission rule.**
- **Part 1 (role): passes.** He was chief executive of Nvidia, which makes the chips frontier models are trained on.
- **Part 2 (looks forward, about AI): fails.** "Five years ahead" judges how far Tesla's hardware leads rivals today. It doesn't say AI will do or ship anything. The years 2020 and 2021 are the dates other carmakers had been giving, not dates Huang sets himself. To get a forecast out of it, you have to infer one: that self-driving will come before 2020. Huang doesn't say that, and the rule doesn't let the ledger supply it.
- **Part 3 (a date):** Because of the above, there is no date of Huang's own to score against.
- **Part 4 (source):** Only a news report, so coverage only at best.

**Not recorded.** This is not the same claim as the 2016-09-28 file ("self-driving cars on road in a couple of years") or any other recorded file.

**Something the reviewer may want to check.** The same page also says, in the reporter's words rather than a quote, that Huang thinks driverless driving is an "AI problem" which "will be solved as early as next year". That is a separate possible claim, but it isn't in Huang's quoted words and it comes only from coverage. "As early as" names only the earliest the thing could come, so reading 3 would most likely treat it as undated as well. The Electrek article or the earnings-call transcript would be the place to look for his own words.
